- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.2), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–5), especially after price spikes; apply downward bias for first 5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts higher than true; cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: model tends to overcorrect after strong moves; apply smoothing or decay factor to recent highs/lows.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with forecast error; when sentiment shifts sharply, reduce forecast confidence and apply lagged adjustment (e.g., 2–3 day delay in reaction).
- If sentiment is neutral or low (0.3–0.6), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3–5 day moving average of past 10–15 days as baseline.
